root_cause.text: The `io_init_req()` function in `io_uring` validated the logical SQ head position instead of the physical SQE index when performing boundary checks for 128-byte SQE operations, allowing users to map a 128-byte operation to the last physical SQE slot via `sq_array` and trigger an out-of-bounds read.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff replaces the logical check `!(ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1))` with a physical index check `(unsigned)(sqe - ctx->sq_sqes) >= ctx->sq_entries - 1` to ensure the SQE does not reside at the last physical slot of the array.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix the contiguous memory check for double-sized SQEs by validating the physical SQE pointer offset instead of the logical queue head.
intent_record.what: Replaces the check on `ctx->cached_sq_head` with a direct pointer arithmetic check comparing the offset of `sqe` from `ctx->sq_sqes` against `ctx->sq_entries - 1`.
intent_record.how: Prevents out-of-bounds access by ensuring that a double-sized (128-byte) SQE has two contiguous entries available at the end of the SQE array, correcting an unreliable index-based wrap-around check.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit introduces the boundary check for 128-byte SQEs in io_init_req() on lines 2198-2199: `!(ctx->cached_sq_head & (ctx->sq_entries - 1))`. This check validates the logical SQ head position (ctx->cached_sq_head) instead of the physical SQE index. Since users can map any physical SQE index to a logical head position via the sq_array, they can map a 128-byte SQE to the last physical slot, bypassing this check and triggering an out-of-bounds read.
